standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (attachable), itechguides.com, twelvetabs.com, lbdsoftware.com, deal.ai (MagHub compare), techradar.com and tomshardware.com (both truncated, so only partly read) and our own 17-inch page. The first four list no 18 or 18.5-inch model, and none of the pages read states a ppi or pixel-count figure for an 18.5-inch panel. deal.ai says only that reviews describe lower pixel density, with no number. ChatGPT's own answer already says 1080p at 18.5 inches looks less sharp than 2K, so the sharpness direction is known; the 119 vs 142 ppi figures, the 10% pixel deficit and the per-model adapter wattage and driver footnotes are new. Our 17-inch page already carries 142 ppi for the 16-inch FOPO rows, so only the 18.5-inch side is new to Dealectric.
decides: It splits the question in two. If the shopper wants 18.5-inch panels, the Aura Studio 18.5 models at $489 to $629 (read today) win on price over the FOPO S999 at $1,099.99, but every multi-screen one needs a driver and a wall adapter. If the shopper wants an extender for an 18-inch laptop, the FOPO S11 and S788 (FOPO's 12–18.5-inch fit range) show 11% more pixels per screen on 16-inch panels, and the S11 is the driver-free row. Our rows therefore honestly win the 'fits an 18-inch laptop' and 'no driver' segments, not 'largest panel'. The footnote for the table: an 18.5-inch panel is 0.59 in taller than a 16-inch 16:10 one but shows fewer pixels.
